verdict: The offer is clear to insiders but the **hero** does not say who it is for or what changes.

findings.title: Hero headline is generic
findings.issue: The headline reads "We build digital experiences", which fits *any* agency and names no audience.
findings.impact_text: Visitors cannot tell in five seconds whether the site is for them.
findings.fix: Rewrite the headline around one outcome for one audience, then support it with a one-line subhead.
findings.evidence: Headline text on the home page, `h1` element.

findings.title: Proof sits far below the claims
findings.issue: Case-study numbers appear three screens below the first claim.
findings.impact_text: Claims are read before proof, so they land as marketing talk.
findings.fix: Move one strong result next to the hero claim and link to the full story at [the case studies](https://ananas-agency.com/work/).

findings.title: Voice shifts between pages
findings.issue: The home page speaks as "we" while service pages use the third person.
findings.fix: Pick the first-person voice and apply it to the service pages.

notes: The page `<title>` says "Ananas Agency | Digital Studio", which repeats the vague hero wording.

extra.title: Voice sample
extra.body: The team says "we" on the About page and "Ananas" in the footer.
